title: POC weekly velocity scrub vs legacy SLA - HelixCare
next_steps: Redwood to share routing playbook + annotated logs sample by 2027-11-03
Customer to run head-to-head 10k qps spike test on dedicated slot next week
Schedule security addendum review (SLA + retention) with legal — target 2027-11-09
action_items: Daniel Park — provide per-model kernel selection notes and expected latency tail by 2027-11-02
Maya Chen — send proposed commercial uplift for dedicated slots and burst buffer by 2027-11-04
Rajiv Menon — share current baseline vendor’s perf logs and load profile CSV by 2027-11-03
Tom Nguyen — validate ingress shaping config and report results by 2027-11-05
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on head-to-head latency/throughput deltas vs HelixCare’s incumbent provider. Redwood presented updated routing changes and quantization profile adjustments; discussed tail latency events during mixed request patterns. Agreed on a controlled 10k qps spike test on Dedicated and a set of logs to be exchanged. Follow-ups: playbook, security/legal sync, and kernel/quant notes from SE.
topics: SLA tail latency and P95/P99 deltas
transcript:
00:00:03 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Halloween, i guess, um we'll try to keep this tight, we have 45 minutes on the calendar. quick roll call?
00:00:10 Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here, sara, tom and priya are on with me.
00:00:14 Sara Lopez: hi all.
00:00:16 Daniel Park: Daniel from Redwood, hi.
00:00:18 Maya Chen: cool. quick agenda: results recap vs baseline, routing changes we pushed yesterday, quant/kv cache notes, open issues and next steps. sound good?
00:00:28 Priya Shah: yep.
00:00:35 Maya Chen: ok, Daniel you wanna kick us off with the numbers?
00:00:38 Daniel Park: sure, i'll share my screen, but i'll just run through the highlights first — overall throughput for our dedicated slot under the standard mixed-profile test was 8.6k rps sustained for 30 minutes, peak bursts to 10.2k for 90s. baseline vendor, from the logs Rajiv sent, was doing 6.4k sustained and peaked to 7.1k on similar workload. latency wise: P50 is comparable, P95 is better for us by about 12 milliseconds, but P99 we still see a tail around 450–520 ms on long-generation calls when the KV cache miss rate spikes.
00:01:32 Rajiv Menon: that tail is our big pain, we target 200ms P99 for inline features otherwise product flags.
00:01:39 Daniel Park: understood, yeah that tail is correlated with mixed context lengths and the cache churn when you have a lot of concurrent users with unique prefixes. we pushed a routing tweak last night that pins hot users to the same instance cohort for 5 minutes — that reduced KV miss rebalance events in the lab by about 38% and reduced tail by roughly 80ms in that scenario.
00:02:06 Tom Nguyen: when you say pinning, do you mean session affinity or more like cache affinity at routing layer?
00:02:12 Daniel Park: cache affinity at the routing layer — sticky routing keyed on the user namespace hash plus a small ttl. not sticky to a single gpu forever, just long enough to amortize the KV warmup.
00:02:25 Sara Lopez: does that cause uneven load across instances? we're worried about hot shard saturation.
00:02:30 Daniel Park: good call — we included a fallback to re-balance if a node's CPU or GPU goes above 78% utilization; then traffic will spill to next-best compatible cohort. so it keeps things balanced.
00:02:44 Maya Chen: and that spillover uses priority tiers, right — production -> reserved -> compatible quantized variants?
00:02:51 Daniel Park: yes, we've got model variant fallback: full fp16 -> int8 quantized -> distilled variant. each has different perf/cost points.
00:02:59 Rajiv Menon: how much quality do we lose on the distilled variant? our product team tested some earlier distillations and it wasn't acceptable for our triage flows.
00:03:07 Daniel Park: fair — distilled is an explicit last resort. our Optimize team ran a small eval on your prompt set; the int8 quantized gives negligible delta for the majority of prompts. distilled shows regressions on a narrow 6% of prompts that are high-context. we can keep those pinned to full fp16.
00:03:28 Priya Shah: can we see that eval report?
00:03:31 Maya Chen: we'll send the annotated eval report, yes. Daniel will attach the per-prompt deltas.
00:03:38 Daniel Park: i'll do that.
00:03:45 Tom Nguyen: back to tail — you mentioned 450–520 ms on P99 for long-gen; any idea which stage is contributing most? is it kernel selection, dispatch or kvcache warmup?
00:03:54 Daniel Park: good question. from tracing, ~40% of the extra tail is KV cache miss and subsequent disk read (when cache cold), ~35% is kernel reorder/compilation overhead for some attention patterns we saw in these prompts, and the remaining 25% is scheduling jitter during spike migrations.
00:04:18 Sara Lopez: compilation overhead? i thought those were JIT'ed once.
00:04:22 Daniel Park: yes normally they're cached; however our workload had a few atypical long sequence variants which forced a new kernel path — and during the first few invocations there's a small compilation and warmup cost. to mitigate we precompiled those kernel paths in the lab and that removed about 90ms.
00:04:40 Rajiv Menon: ok that helps. so end-to-end, with pinning + precompile + kv tweaks, what will P99 look like?
00:04:48 Daniel Park: in our next lab run we projected P99 around 260–290ms on the mixed-profile, which gets you much closer to the 200ms target — still slightly above for the largest gen cases but within the buffer where we can use model-level routing to keep high-risk flows on fp16.
00:05:03 Maya Chen: small note: those projections assume the ingress shaping matches the profile you shared last week. if actual traffic has higher unique prefix churn the tail could widen.
00:05:15 Tom Nguyen: that's on us — our burst simulator might underrepresent the real user churn. we'll re-run with higher entropy.
00:05:22 Sara Lopez: what's the cost delta vs baseline when you run dedicated with these optimizations?
00:05:28 Daniel Park: good question — ballpark our int8 quant and better batching reduces per-token compute cost by 18% compared to baseline run; but reserved dedicated slot costs are a separate line item. using our burst buffer policy instead of standing up extra capacity cuts the incremental monthly cost by ~24% compared to simply provisioning +25% headroom. overall unit cost we estimate is ~12% lower than incumbent for matched latency SLO.
00:05:51 Rajiv Menon: and that's not accounting for their volume discounts?
00:05:54 Daniel Park: correct, that's a like-for-like technical unit cost estimate; commercial terms can change effective price.
00:05:59 Priya Shah: any security or compliance caveats with sticky routing or cached KV? we have to track residency.
00:06:07 Daniel Park: KV entries are encrypted at rest and in-flight; sticky routing does not change residency — data stays in your VPC for private deployment or in our dedicated tenant for Redwood Dedicated. audit logs are emitted for routing decisions, which we can show in the console.
00:06:21 Maya Chen: lena, we should note to attach the audit log sample.
00:06:24 Lena Ortiz: noted. i'll include the routing decision log snippet and retention options.
00:06:30 00:06:31 Rajiv Menon: quick question on the 10.2k peak you mentioned — that's sustained over 90 seconds, but our real spikes are shorter and higher, down to 30s spikes up to 12k. how do you handle very short spikes?
00:06:45 Daniel Park: for sub-1-minute spikes we rely on prewarmed burst slots and rapid autoscaler heuristics. the burst buffer can deliver up to a 4x burst above baseline for up to 2 minutes before we spin extra nodes. there's a cold-start tradeoff if the spike persists longer.
00:07:02 Tom Nguyen: can we test the 30s 12k scenario in staging?
00:07:05 Daniel Park: absolutely — that's part of the next-step controlled spike. we'd request a test window where you run the 30s spike at 12k, then a sustained 3-minute 9k to observe spillover behavior.
00:07:18 Maya Chen: ok, Rajiv can you confirm willingness to run that next week?
00:07:21 Rajiv Menon: yes, we can. we'll run it monday morning.
00:07:25 Maya Chen: great. any other performance anomalies you saw?
00:07:30 Sara Lopez: one more — memory pressure during long multi-turn dialogs caused occasional retries in the SE logs.
00:07:36 Daniel Park: we saw that too. that's the kernel path + kv growth issue. we applied a soft cap on KV per-session and evict older prefixes after threshold — it reduced OOM-like retries in lab. we'll push a more conservative cap in staging for your spike test.
00:07:51 Priya Shah: perfect. on observability — can we get per-token cost breakdown and token-level latency in the console?
00:07:59 Maya Chen: yes, the console exposes per-route token cost and latency; we'll also share a csv export option.
00:08:05 Lena Ortiz: i'll add sample exports to the next email.
00:08:10 Daniel Park: i'll also include the kernel selection matrix and the precompiled path list — that should help your infra team correlate traces.
00:08:18 Rajiv Menon: switching gears to baseline comparison — we sent over their perf logs, there are a few spikes where their P99 was 1.3s and in your latest run we saw 520ms, is that directly comparable?
00:08:29 Daniel Park: mostly yes, but small differences: their run used fewer warmers and no precompiled kernel runs; they also had a slightly different request mix — more long generations. we normalized where possible but not perfect.
00:08:41 Sara Lopez: would you be comfortable providing a side-by-side CSV with normalized fields? it's easier for exec review.
00:08:47 Daniel Park: yes, we'll prepare a normalized head-to-head CSV and include notes on assumptions.
00:08:53 Maya Chen: action:item — Daniel to send normalized CSV and kernel notes.
00:08:58 00:09:01 Priya Shah: on the legal/commercial side, we need a draft SLA that includes the fallback playbook — incase of tail violations what are credits, what's the rollback cadence, etc.
00:09:11 Maya Chen: i'll surface that to commercial, we'll propose language and policy.
00:09:15 Rajiv Menon: also retention — we need 7 years for some audit traces which might be above your default; can you support long-term archival?
00:09:24 Lena Ortiz: we support extended retention as an add-on; we'll include cost and retention tiers in the package.
00:09:30 Tom Nguyen: one operational question — when you spill to quantized variants, is that transparent to downstream telemetry or does it change model tags?
00:09:38 Daniel Park: we emit model_variant tag in traces and in metrics, so your telemetry can filter by variant for accuracy trend lines.
00:09:46 Priya Shah: good.
00:09:49 Maya Chen: any blockers to scheduling the controlled spike test?
00:09:53 Rajiv Menon: none on our side, monday morning PST is fine.
00:09:58 Maya Chen: excellent. recap — playbook and annotated logs from us, normalized CSV and kernel notes from Daniel, HelixCare runs the 30s/12k spike then 3-minute sustain, legal sync for SLA/retention. anything else?
00:10:14 Sara Lopez: one very small ask — can you add an example of the routing decision blob we can forward to our compliance team, anonymized?
00:10:22 Daniel Park: yes, we'll anonymize and strip PII.
00:10:27 Maya Chen: perfect. ok we'll wrap up, thanks everyone.
00:10:31 Rajiv Menon: thanks.
00:10:33 Tom Nguyen: thanks.
00:10:35 Maya Chen: bye.

Note: transcript truncated for brevity — full meeting had troubleshooting sub-discussions, quick live demo of trace view, and confirmation of next test windows. Transcription includes some mis-hearings (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes transcribed as "k v cash").
